docs.title: SplatXR Toolkit
docs.text:
The SplatXR Toolkit provides building blocks for developing XR (AR/VR/MR) applications that integrate 3D Gaussian Splatting for rendering objects and environments, with support for physics-based interactions, visual effects, and reality blending.

v0.0.2 Unity 2022.0+ (tested on 6.2)

docs.title: What is SplatXR?
docs.text:
SplatXR accelerates prototyping and research for XR experiences that leverage 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for immersive, interactive spaces. It's built around a modular building block system spanning four layers of a multi-layer reality framework:

  • Rendering layer — GPU-optimized, on-headset visualization of Gaussian splats.
  • Physics layer — collision detection and physical interaction through mesh-augmented splats.
  • Effects layer — visual enhancements like disintegration and digital rain.
  • Blending layer — portal-like effects and compositing between virtual splat scenes and real spaces.

Building blocks can be accessed through the SplatXR Building Blocks Panel (SplatXR > Building Blocks Panel) and applied to splat GameObjects individually or in combination.

docs.title: Platform Support
docs.text:
SplatXR primarily targets and is developed for the Meta Quest 3. It has also been tested on Apple Vision Pro. It will likely work on other Unity-based XR headsets. We welcome contributions for support on other AR/VR platforms.

Meta Quest 3 — fully supported Apple Vision Pro — tested

docs.title: Building Blocks
docs.text:
Jump into a specific building block to see its parameters and usage:

  • Splat Renderer

    Core rendering for Gaussian splats, with Base and LoD modes.

  • Splat Physics

    Collision meshes, rigid bodies, and shadow casting from splats.

  • Splat Effects

    Disintegrate, radial reveal, and digital rain shader effects.

  • Splat Blending

    Portal windows blending splat spaces with passthrough reality.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
We welcome contributions from the community! Technical support and maintenance from the original authors will be limited. We encourage the community to:

  • Contribute features or improvements via pull requests.
  • Improve or add to the documentation.
  • Answer questions and help triage issues on GitHub.

Head over to the SplatXR repository to open an issue, start a discussion, or submit a pull request.

docs.title: Splat count limitations
docs.text:
There is a performance limitation of approximately 200,000 splats per scene. Exceeding this limit may cause performance degradation. When working with large splat files, consider:

  • Decimating your source splat data.
  • Using the LoD Renderer to swap lower-detail versions at distance.

The limitation is primarily the number/FOV/layering of visible splats in a scene's rendered view. Further optimizations are under development.

docs.title: Possible slow-down in in-editor viewing
docs.text: When viewing splats in the Unity editor, it's recommended to enable the "Remove Outline" option in the in-editor viewer for better rendering performance while selecting the splat in the editor.

docs.title: Scene-based meshing detail
docs.text:
Scene-based meshing (when using Splat Type: Space in physics generation) may not produce highly detailed meshes. For objects requiring detailed collision meshes, use Splat Type: Object instead.

Camera distance and performance

Avoid keeping the camera/headset extremely close to splat surfaces/objects — close proximity can cause rendering slowdowns and stuttering due to the high density of splats being processed. Maintain a reasonable viewing distance from splat objects for optimal performance.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release of the toolkit from the SplatXR Releases page and unzip it.
  2. Open your Unity project.
  3. Go to Window > Package Manager.
  4. Click the + button in the top-left corner.
  5. Select Add package from disk....
  6. Navigate to the unzipped toolkit folder and select the package.json file.
  7. Unity will import the package and it will appear in the Package Manager under In Project.
  8. Open SplatXR > Building Blocks Panel from the Unity menu to view the SplatXR panel.

Install the meshing tool

The Splat Physics building block needs the SplatXR meshing tool to generate collision meshes. Install it for your platform:

  • macOS: link coming soon (TBD)
  • Windows: link coming soon (TBD)

Next

Head to the Quickstart to import your first Gaussian splat.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
To quickly import a Gaussian splat into your Unity scene:

  1. Open SplatXR > Building Blocks Panel from the Unity menu.
  2. Select the Splat Renderer building block from the panel.
  3. In the Object Name field, enter a name for your splat object.
  4. Keep Renderer set to Base Renderer.
  5. Click the folder icon next to Input Splat File (PLY) and select your .ply file containing the Gaussian splat data.
  6. Click Add to Scene to create the splat object in your scene.

You're set

Your splat object should now be rendered in the scene and ready for further additions using the other building blocks — physics, effects, and blending.

docs.title: Technical Evaluation Suite
docs.text:
Standalone Meta Quest 3

SplatXR comes with a companion evaluation suite for benchmarking the toolkit on standalone headsets. Its main focus is the runtime renderer: it measures rendering performance across splat objects, indoor scenes, and outdoor scenes at multiple splat counts and viewpoints. The suite also times splat import, splat-to-mesh conversion, and on-headset object reconstruction.

All benchmarks were run on-device on a standalone Meta Quest 3 across repeated trials. Detailed methodology and results are reported in the paper.

The evaluation suite will be open-source and available soon, so you can reproduce these benchmarks or run them on your own splats and hardware.

splatxr/splatxr-evals · Coming soon

docs.title: Splat Blending
docs.text:
System for creating portal effects where splat spaces can be viewed through virtual windows, blending reality with the splat spaces.

Blending layer Meta SDK · Apple Vision Pro (untested)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Use this building block to create portal effects where users can look through a virtual window into a different splat space.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Garden portal: a botanical garden splat seen through a window in a real wall. Room portal: a living room splat blends into the real space through soft portal edges.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description XR Platform Choose Meta SDK or Apple Vision Pro. Apple Vision Pro is untested, and only fully immersive (Metal) apps are expected to work. Center Eye Camera The headset's center eye camera. You can assign the camera itself (CenterEyeAnchor for Meta SDK), the Meta camera rig (e.g. the [Building Block] Camera Rig), or any parent of a camera tagged MainCamera.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The block:

  1. Adds a MetaSplatBlendingPortal object to the scene, with a sample portal plane that uses the Blending Portal material.
  2. Adds LeftEyeBlending and RightEyeBlending cameras under the center eye camera.
  3. Creates a "BlendingWorld" layer if it doesn't exist. The left and right eye cameras render only that layer, and the center eye camera stops rendering it.

Objects on the "BlendingWorld" layer are only visible through the portal. Put everything you want seen through the portal, such as a splat space, on that layer. To make your own portal window, apply the Blending Portal material to any mesh.

Adding the block again with the same center eye camera reuses the existing portal and eye cameras instead of creating duplicates. There is a controllable Edge Softness parameter in the material shader to create a vignette effect along the border of the portal window.

docs.title: Splat Effects
docs.text:
Visual effects system for applying shader-based effects to Gaussian splats, including disintegration, radial reveal, and digital rain.

Effects layer Requires Splat Renderer

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Add this building block to the parent splat GameObject to create dynamic visual effects. Useful for transitions, interactions, or stylized appearances.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Disintegrate: a plant assembles from particles, then breaks apart. Digital Rain: splats rain down and assemble into a room.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Target Splat The parent splat GameObject created by the Splat Renderer building block (the one with the splat_renderer child). Effect Selection Disintegrate: particle-based disintegration effect.Radial Reveal: spherical reveal/hide effect from a point.Digital Rain: splats rain down and assemble into the object.Custom Shader: use your own effect shader. Custom Shader (Custom Shader only) The shader to apply. Required when Custom Shader is selected.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The block swaps the shader on the splat_renderer child's material for the effect shader, and adds a SplatEffectsBuildingBlock component to the parent object. The effect starts off.

Each effect runs across a timeline from 0 to 1. Control it from the SplatEffectsBuildingBlock component in the Inspector:

Field Description Is Effect Active Turn on to play the effect, off to stop it. Time Multiplier Playback speed. At 1, the effect takes 1 second from start to end. Loop Effect Restart from 0 after reaching 1. Otherwise the effect holds at 1.

From a script, call StartEffect(), StopEffect(), SetTime(float) (clamped to 0–1), and SetLoop(bool).

docs.title: Writing a custom effect shader
docs.text:
Each frame the component sets two material properties, which your shader should declare:

  • _EffectActive: 1 while the effect is playing, otherwise 0.
  • _EffectTime: the current position on the 0–1 timeline.

Start from one of the built-in shaders in Runtime/SplatXRBuildingBlocks/Effects/Shaders so your shader keeps the splat rendering code.

docs.title: Splat Physics
docs.text:
Generates collision meshes from Gaussian splats to enable physics interactions, rigid body dynamics, and shadow casting.

Physics layer Requires Splat Renderer

Requires the meshing tool

This building block needs the SplatXR meshing tool. See Installation for the macOS and Windows downloads.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Apply this building block to an existing splat renderer object when you need collision detection, physics collisions, or shadow casting.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Target Splat Existing splat GameObject created by the Splat Renderer building block. You can select the parent object or its splat_renderer child; physics is always added to the parent. Splat Type Object (detailed mesh for props/items) or Space (simplified mesh for rooms/environments). Mesh Threshold (Object type) Density threshold for mesh generation. Range 0–1, default 0.5. Gaussian Mesh Scale (Object type) Scale factor for individual gaussians during meshing. Larger values help for sparser gaussians. Range 0–2, default 1.5. Mesh Base Flattening Enable to flatten the bottom of the mesh (useful for placing objects on surfaces). Flatten Percentage (If flattening enabled) Amount to flatten. Range 0–1, default 0.05. Flatten Axis (If flattening enabled) Axis direction for flattening, generally the base (X, Y, Z, -X, -Y, -Z).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Object meshing creates more detailed meshes suitable for interactive props, while Space meshing creates simplified meshes for environment boundaries.

The physics mesh, collider, and Rigidbody go on the splat's parent object, not on the splat_renderer child that draws it. Adding a mesh to the child would replace the splat's own mesh and hide it. If you select the child, the block moves the physics to its parent and logs a message. If the selected object draws the splat and has no parent, the block shows an error instead. In that case, recreate the splat with the Splat Renderer building block.

Known limitation

Scene-based meshing (Splat Type: Space) may not produce highly detailed meshes. For objects requiring detailed collision meshes, use Splat Type: Object instead. See the FAQ.

docs.title: Splat Renderer
docs.text:
Core rendering component for displaying Gaussian splats with our stand-alone on-device rendering pipeline.

Rendering layer Foundational block

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This is the foundational building block for splat rendering. Maximum recommended splat count per scene is under 200k for optimal performance, but this may vary depending on target hardware.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Object Name Name for the splat GameObject. Renderer Choose between Base Renderer (single PLY file) or LoD Renderer (multiple detail levels for distance-based optimization). Input Splat File (PLY) (Base Renderer) Path to the splat .ply file. High / Medium / Low Detail Splat (LoD Renderer) Paths to different detail level PLY files.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Start with Base Renderer for single splats. Use LoD Renderer when working with large scenes where different detail levels are needed at varying distances to maintain performance. Simply import a .ply file and the toolkit script will create a usplat CSV file, which is automatically assigned to the renderer script.

The building block creates a parent GameObject (named after Object Name) with a splat_renderer child that holds the renderer component and draws the splat. Move, rotate, or scale the parent rather than the child.

Tip

Enable "Remove Outline" in the in-editor viewer when selecting a splat object for smoother editor performance. See the FAQ for more details.

docs.title: LoD distances
docs.text:
The LoD Renderer draws one detail level per distance band from the camera. The defaults are below; change them with Lod Distance High and Lod Distance Medium on the LoDRendererSplatXR component of the splat_renderer child.

Distance from camera Detail level Up to 2 m High 2 m – 5 m Medium Beyond 5 m Low

You don't need all three files. If a level has no file, its band falls back to the next coarser level that has one, then to a finer one. For example, with only High and Low assigned, the 2–5 m band uses Low. Removing a file from a level in the Inspector stops that level from rendering.

docs.title: Splat file format
docs.text:
The usplat CSV has a header line, then one splat per line with 13 comma-separated numbers:

x,y,z,opacity,f_dc_0,f_dc_1,f_dc_2,cov0,cov1,cov2,cov3,cov4,cov5

Lines with fewer than 13 columns or non-numeric values are skipped, and the rest of the file still loads. The Console shows a warning with the number of skipped lines and the first one's line number.

docs.title: Material and Color Controls
docs.text:
Each splat gets its own material, saved as Assets/Materials/SplatMaterials/SplatMaterial_<Object Name>.mat and assigned to the splat_renderer child. It uses the SplatXR/SplatShader shader. Editing it changes only that splat, and the original splat file isn't modified.

Select the material (or the splat_renderer child) to adjust its photometric properties in the Inspector: Color Tint, Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Temperature (cool to warm), and Transparency. Scale Factor scales the splat's size. At their defaults (white tint, 0 temperature, everything else 1), the splat looks unchanged.

The shader applies them in this order: color correction (below), tint, temperature, saturation, then contrast and brightness.

docs.title: Auto color correction with passthrough
docs.text:
A splat captured at a different time or under different lighting often looks off next to the real room seen through passthrough. The Splat Passthrough Color Adjustment component (SplatPassthroughColorAdjustment) matches the splat's colors to the real environment.

To set it up:

  1. Select the splat object and choose Add Component > SplatXR > Splat Passthrough Color Adjustment.
  2. Assign a Splat Render Image: a capture of the splat as it renders, such as a screenshot from Unity.
  3. Assign a Passthrough Image: a passthrough camera image of the real space the splat should match.
  4. Assign the splat's material as the Target Material.
  5. Click Apply Color Correction in the component.

Note

Both images need Read/Write enabled in their texture import settings.

The component compares the mean and spread of each color channel (R, G, B) in the two images and computes an ASC CDL correction (slope, offset, and power) that maps the splat image's colors onto the passthrough image's. Values are clamped to a safe range so a mismatched image pair can't blow out the splat.

docs.title: How the material is updated
docs.text:
The correction is stored on the material, not in the splat file. Apply Color Correction writes the results to the material's ASC CDL Color Correction properties (ASC-CDL Slope, ASC-CDL Offset, and ASC-CDL Power), sets Enable ASC-CDL to 1, and saves the material asset. Because the values live on the material:

  • The correction stays applied after you leave Play mode and in builds, even if you disable or remove the component.
  • You can undo it with Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS).
  • You can fine-tune it on top with the color controls above, since the shader applies the correction first.

To compare with and without the correction, set Enable ASC-CDL on the material to 0 (off) or 1 (on). This keeps the computed values. Reset Color Correction in the component returns slope, offset, and power to neutral and turns Enable ASC-CDL off.

docs.title: Cropping
docs.text:
Cropping hides splats outside a box, which is useful for removing background clutter or floaters around a captured object. Open the Cropping Controls foldout on the renderer component on the splat_renderer child:

Field Description Enable Cropping Turn cropping on or off. Crop Bounds Min / Max Opposite corners of the crop box, in the splat's local space. Default (-5, -5, -5) to (5, 5, 5). Crop Bounds Rotation Rotation of the crop box, in degrees. Show Crop Bounds Draw the crop box as a yellow wireframe in the Scene view (while cropping is on).

Only splats inside the box are drawn, and the splat updates as soon as you change the box. Cropping doesn't change the splat file, so turning it off brings every splat back. It works with both the Base and LoD Renderers.
